newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power weaker amid lower demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power weaker amid lower demand.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West eased slightly amid weaker demand in the Southwest and selling ahead of the holiday weekend, trade sources said Thursday.
"We saw a few people looking to get rid of Saturday power," said a trader at a California utility.
Next-day California-Oregon border (COB) power was last quoted $18.75-19.25 per megawatt hour (MWh), down slightly from $19.00-19.50 on Wednesday.
COB for the balance of October was seen bid at $17.50.
Mid-Columbia for Friday was quoted around $18.00 per MWh and $17.00-17.50 for Saturday.
Next-day Palo Verde was last quoted $19.50-21.00 per MWh, down from $21.00-23.00 on Wednesday.
Traders cited cooler Southwest temperatures and the impending restart of several power generation units as factors putting downward pressure on prices.

The 350 MW unit 2 at the San Juan, N.M., power station was expected to resume operations late today, while the 1,080 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in California is scheduled to begin the restart process Friday.
A 750 MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired plant in Washington is also expected to restart Friday.
Palo Verde for November was last quoted $16.90-17.00 per MWh, down from $17.40-17.85 on Wednesday. November COB was quoted $17.45-17.60, compared with above $18.00 on Wednesday.
